added_models.model: Cynomolgus monkey repeat-dose toxicology of R1507/teprotumumab

safety.note: Roche's GLP monkey toxicology of R1507 (teprotumumab) began November 2004 and supported its oncology trials; no comparison with patients yet.
safety.short: Monkey GLP toxicology of R1507 begins
safety.quote: Ro 485-8696/F01-01(huMAb-IGF-1R): A 7-Week Intermittent Intravenous Toxicity, Toxicokinetic, and Immunogenicity Study with Ro 485-8696/F01-01 (huMAb-IGF-1R) in Cynomolgus Monkeys with an 8-Week Recovery Period
safety.confidence_note: Study title and initiation date (November 3, 2004) read in the FDA pharmacology/toxicology review text.
safety.judgement: Opening entry at the first GLP monkey study of a member antibody (R1507 = teprotumumab, Ro 485-8696).

safety.note: FDA: monkeys predicted weight loss and low ALP but not hyperglycemia, infusion reactions or IBD flares; hyperglycemia is an on-target harm also seen with members in NSCLC.
safety.quote: the monkey model predicted the clinical reduced weight gain/weight loss and decreased serum ALP, but not the clinical infusion reactions, exacerbation of inflammatory bowel disease, or hyperglycemia.
safety.confidence_note: Review dated January 2020 (approval Jan 2020) but filed under nda/2021, so dated to 2021 posting; exact posting date not verified. Comparison made in TED patients, imported.
safety.judgement: Monkeys can show glucose dysregulation, so their silence on hyperglycemia is a scored miss, not a species limit. Hyperglycemia is on-target (IGF1R/IR), so the harm pools across modality; also seen with cixutumumab (Novello 2017, Argiris 2017) and dalotuzumab (Huang 2016) in NSCLC. Partial match on weight/ALP noted.
safety.magnitude_basis: presence of hyperglycemia, infusion reactions and IBD exacerbation in patients vs none in monkeys

added_models.model: 22-line NSCLC cell panel treated with R1507 (total IGF-1R as response marker)

efficacy.note: Panel predicted high total tumour IGF-1R picks R1507 responders; Roche's biomarker analysis of the R1507+erlotinib trial (Habben 2011) could not be read verbatim.
efficacy.quote: In NSCLC cell lines, high levels of total IGF-1R are associated with moderate sensitivity to R1507. These results suggest a possible enrichment strategy for clinical trials with anti-IGF-1R therapy.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Patient-side test is Habben et al., J Clin Oncol 29:15_suppl 7584 (ASCO 2011, doi:10.1200/jco.2011.29.15_suppl.7584): a search summary says IGF1R H-score subgroups showed no PFS difference, which would make this contra, but the abstract text was not retrievable (403), so no quote and the status stays untested.
efficacy.judgement: Cell lines in vitro are not an enum kind; ex_vivo used as the closest non-animal kind. Ramalingam 2011 cites this panel but does not compare it with trial biomarker data (biomarkers 'reported separately'), so it is not a stated comparison.
efficacy.population: NSCLC, total IGF-1R high vs low

considered_not_added: Forest 2015 Mol Cancer Res (PMID 26263910): lung adenocarcinoma PDX where total insulin receptor predicts cixutumumab resistance; no member NSCLC trial tested IR expression, so no patient comparison.

Serum free IGF-1 as response marker (Huang 2016 dalotuzumab discussion; Habben 2011 R1507 abstract summary): patient-side hypotheses with no preclinical model making the prediction in this class; Habben text unverifiable.
Cynomolgus monkey tolerability margin for dose: no model-stated effective exposure to pair with; the draft's dose cell already covers the xenograft side.
Ganitumab in SCLC (Glisson 2017) and cixutumumab in SCLC (ECOG E1508): small-cell lung cancer is a different disease from this tile's MONDO.
Figitumumab NSCLC models and phase 3 failures: not a member drug.
LUMVOA (BLA 761530) review in the bundle: not a member drug of this tile.
In-silico/QSP dose models, patient-derived organoids or ex-vivo patient tumour sensitivity, PDX co-clinical trials, human genetic IGF1R models: none found for member drugs in NSCLC.

Gong 2009 panel read as a class-level prediction (only 5/22 lines sensitive, so little benefit in unselected NSCLC): the paper frames it as an enrichment strategy, not a prediction of no unselected benefit, so not scored at class level.
